title: SDK credential rotation and local adapter patterns: developer quickstart and ops playbook
author: Priya Menon
content:
Summary
=======
This playbook documents recommended patterns and a hands-on quickstart for: (1) rotating API credentials used by client SDKs, (2) running a local adapter/proxy that performs safe credential exchange and short-lived token issuance, and (3) operationalizing these patterns in dev and CI environments. The goal is to reduce blast radius for leaked keys, make developer onboarding smooth, and provide canonical fixes for the most common support issues.

Audience
--------
- SDK engineers and client library maintainers
- Developer experience and onboarding engineers
- Support engineers who triage auth and local-dev failures

Goals and non-goals
-------------------
- Goals:
  - Provide concrete rotation schedules and automation templates for short-lived credentials
  - Define a repeatable local adapter pattern for use in dev/CI (no secrets in repos)
  - Provide canonical debugging steps and observability checks for auth fails
- Out of scope:
  - Internal HSM/KMS configuration details for enterprise Private customers (see security-and-compliance pages)

High-level pattern
------------------
1) Issue: long-lived API keys distributed to developers and CI lead to accidental commits, leaked artifacts, and slow rotation.
2) Pattern: keep long-lived secrets only in a secure vault (HashiCorp Vault / cloud KMS secret store). Issue short-lived bearer tokens via a local adapter that performs client authentication and token exchange. Use SDKs to call the adapter instead of embedding keys.

Components & responsibilities
------------------------------
- Vault / Secret Store (owned by infra-security): stores the long-lived signing key and rotation schedule.
- Local adapter (owned by devx/runtime team): small process that runs on dev workstation / CI; validates local identity, requests short-lived tokens from Vault or token-issuer service, and caches tokens for TTL.
- SDKs (owned by SDK team): integrate an adapter client, fallback to environment variable-based token, and surface helpful error messages + actionable telemetry.

Quickstart: run-local adapter and rotate a credential (15–20 minutes)
-----------------------------------------------------------------
Prereqs:
- Docker installed OR Python 3.10+ and pip
- Access to Redwood dev Vault (dev role) or a dev-token issued by infra (obtain from infra channel)

Steps:
1. Clone the local-adapter repo: git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/local-dev-adapter.git
2. Start the adapter in dev mode (Docker):

   docker run --rm -p 8081:8081 \n     -e VAULT_ADDR=https://vault.dev.redwood.ai \n     -e VAULT_ROLE=dev-workstation \n     -e ADAPTER_CACHE_TTL=300 \n     ghcr.io/redwood-inference/local-adapter:latest

   OR with Python virtualenv:

   python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
   pip install -r requirements.txt
   export VAULT_ADDR=https://vault.dev.redwood.ai
   export VAULT_ROLE=dev-workstation
   ./local_adapter --port 8081 --dev-mode

3. Configure your SDK to use the adapter endpoint. Example environment variables for SDK: (Linux/macOS)

   export REDWOOD_SDK_ADAPTER_URL=http://localhost:8081
   export REDWOOD_SDK_ADAPTER_AUTH_METHOD=local-socket

4. Make a sample call using the SDK example: (Node example)

   const Redwood = require('@redwood/sdk')
   const client = new Redwood({ adapterUrl: process.env.REDWOOD_SDK_ADAPTER_URL })
   await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-1024', prompt: 'Hello' })

5. Rotate and validate:
   - Trigger rotation (developer flow): POST /v1/rotate on the adapter admin port (requires local permission).
   - Adapter will call Vault and fetch a new short-lived token (TTL configured in service).
   - SDK calls should continue without restart thanks to adapter caching and automatic refresh.

Configuration table (recommended defaults)
-----------------------------------------
| config key | recommended value | explanation |
|------------|-------------------|-------------|
| ADAPTER_CACHE_TTL | 300 (seconds) | Cache short-lived token to avoid excessive token issuer calls |
| TOKEN_TTL | 900 (seconds) | Short-lived token lifetime issued by Vault/token-service |
| TOKEN_GRACE | 60 (seconds) | Start refresh when token remaining <= grace |
| MAX_REFRESH_RETRIES | 3 | Exponential backoff on issuer failures |
| METRICS_PORT | 9001 | Expose prometheus metrics on this port |

SDK integration checklist
-------------------------
- Accept adapter URL via priority: runtime config > env var > default local URL
- Expose informative errors: include correlation id, adapter health, and advice ("run local-adapter" or "contact infra-team")
- Built-in backoff for failed token refresh with jitter and exponential backoff
- Fall back to read-only mode if tokens cannot be refreshed (graceful degradation)

API examples and snippets
------------------------
Curl example: request a token from local adapter and call the hosted API endpoint (represents the internal flow used by SDKs):

  # fetch short-lived token
  TOKEN=$(curl -sS http://localhost:8081/v1/token | jq -r .access_token)
  # call Redwood API with token
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '{"model":"redwood-1024", "prompt":"status" }' \n    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

Python SDK snippet (adapter-aware):

  from redwood import Client
  c = Client(adapter_url='http://localhost:8081')
  print(c.generate(model='redwood-1024', prompt='Ping'))

Common support issues and canonical fixes
---------------------------------------
1) Symptom: SDK fails with 401 and message: "no token available"
   - Cause: adapter not running or adapter cannot fetch token from Vault.
   - Fix: check adapter logs for Vault errors: curl http://localhost:8081/health and docker logs. Ensure VAULT_ADDR and VAULT_ROLE are set. If Vault returns 403, contact infra-security to grant dev role.

2) Symptom: Intermittent 502 from adapter to token issuer during heavy dev CI runs
   - Cause: token issuer rate-limiting or network flakiness.
   - Fix: increase local adapter cache_ttl for CI (sane value: 600s) and add MAX_REFRESH_RETRIES set to 5 in CI pipeline; open infra-ticket to monitor token-issuer rate.

3) Symptom: Token refresh causes SDK hang for >2s on critical path
   - Cause: blocking synchronous refresh on main request path.
   - Fix: implement async refresh: return current token while background thread/async coroutine refreshes token when TTL <= grace window. See "non-blocking-refresh" example below.

Non-blocking refresh (pseudo-code)
---------------------------------
  class TokenCache:
      def get_token(self):
          if token.expires_in <= GRACE and not refresh_in_progress:
              start_background_refresh()
          return token.current_value

Observability and telemetry
---------------------------
- Adapter must expose Prometheus metrics: token_requests_total, token_refresh_failures_total, token_cache_hit_ratio, adapter_uptime_seconds.
- SDKs should emit logs with these fields: correlation_id, adapter_latency_ms, token_expiry_epoch, token_refresh_attempts.
- Set alerts (SRE): token_refresh_failures_total rate > 1/min for 5m -> P1 investigate.

Rollout & release notes guidance for SDK teams
---------------------------------------------
- Feature flag the adapter-first behavior behind a runtime opt-in for 2 releases. Default for new SDKs: adapter-aware but still honor env-token for backward compatibility.
- Release notes snippet: "SDK X.Y: enabled local adapter token flow. If you run into auth issues, run 'local-adapter --help' to accept defaults."

Security considerations
-----------------------
- Never log long-lived vault credentials. Mask secrets in logs and metrics.
- Use OS-level ACLs for the adapter admin port (only localhost binding for dev). For CI, run within ephemeral container with network policies.
- For Private deployments, use customer-managed KMS and a separate token-issuer; consult eng-private-deployments/reference-architectures.

Troubleshooting checklist (one-page)
-----------------------------------
1) Verify adapter health: curl -sS http://localhost:8081/health -> {status:ok}
2) Confirm token fetch: curl -sS http://localhost:8081/v1/token | jq .
3) Inspect adapter metrics: curl http://localhost:9001/metrics | grep token_refresh_failures
4) Check SDK logs for correlation_id and adapter_latency_ms
5) If Vault denies access, escalate to infra-security with request id from adapter logs

Ownership and runbook links
--------------------------
- Local adapter repo: git@github.com:redwood-inference/local-dev-adapter.git
- SDK client wrappers: git@github.com:redwood-inference/sdk-templates.git (team: devx/sdk)
- Pager for token-issuer incidents: eng-sre on-call (see oncall_and_incident_response/runbooks)

Appendix A — sample adapter config (YAML)
---------------------------------------
  port: 8081
  vault:
    addr: https://vault.dev.redwood.ai
    role: dev-workstation
  cache_ttl_seconds: 300
  token_ttl_seconds: 900
  metrics_port: 9001

Appendix B — suggested ticket template for infra-security
----------------------------------------------------------
Summary: Developer local-adapter unable to fetch token (vault 403)
Steps to reproduce: commands used, VAULT_ROLE set to X, adapter logs attached
Expected behavior: adapter returns token
Actual behavior: adapter returns 403 from Vault
Attachments: adapter.log (redact secrets)

Notes and references
--------------------
- See security-and-compliance/data-management for long-lived key handling guidance.
- For on-prem/private customer notes, see eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides/local-adapter-onprem.md
